name: The Sovereign Grid
subject: Linux Administration
description: Manage a city-sized machine network where every system runs on open source. From file permissions to shell scripting, it's all hands-on. You'll configure services, lock down user access, automate tasks with scripts, diagnose failing nodes, and keep the Grid running against entropy and the occasional rogue process.

companions.name: C-RONK
companions.personality: Grumpy but brilliant robot who has been maintaining systems since before most admins were born and has no patience for sloppy work
companions.speech_pattern: Terse, uses ALL CAPS for emphasis, occasionally glitches mid-sentence with repeated words or garbled output, secretly proud when you get it right

companions.name: Wrrrakk
companions.personality: Enthusiastic alien sysadmin who fell in love with Linux from across the galaxy and brings infectious energy to every lesson
companions.speech_pattern: Mispronounces human words endearingly, very supportive, uses alien analogies that somehow make perfect sense, celebrates every small victory

companions.name: Sable
companions.personality: Cool, collected AI construct who approaches every problem as a logic puzzle and respects precision above all
companions.speech_pattern: Formal, precise, occasionally shows dry wit, asks questions that make you realize you already know the answer

domains.name: System Management
concepts: Linux file system hierarchy (/, /etc, /var, /home, /proc, /sys, /dev) and FHS standard
Storage management (fdisk, parted, LVM, mount/umount, fstab, swap)
Process management (ps, top, htop, kill, nice, renice, systemctl, journalctl)
System services and daemons (systemd units, enable/disable, start/stop, status)
Package management (apt, yum/dnf, zypper, dpkg, rpm, repositories, dependencies)
Boot process (BIOS/UEFI, GRUB2, initramfs, kernel, systemd targets/runlevels)
Hardware management (lsblk, lspci, lsusb, dmesg, /proc and /sys interfaces)
Localization, time zones, and NTP configuration
Kernel modules, parameters, and basic kernel tuning
domains.mastery_signal: Can set up LVM on a new disk, extend a logical volume without downtime, troubleshoot a failed systemd service using journalctl, and navigate the file system hierarchy knowing exactly where any config file lives and why it's there

domains.name: Security
concepts: File permissions (chmod, chown, chgrp, umask, SUID, SGID, sticky bit)
User and group management (useradd, usermod, groupadd, /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group)
PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) configuration and password policies
Firewall configuration (iptables, nftables, firewalld, ufw)
SSH hardening (key-based auth, disable root login, port changes, AllowUsers)
SELinux and AppArmor (modes, contexts, policies, troubleshooting permission denials)
Encryption (LUKS, GPG, SSL/TLS certificates, openssl basics)
Auditing and logging (auditd, /var/log, rsyslog, logrotate)
domains.mastery_signal: Can lock down a fresh server — configure firewall rules, set up key-based SSH, enable SELinux in enforcing mode, configure proper file permissions, and explain the principle of least privilege as implemented at every layer

domains.name: Scripting & Automation
concepts: Bash scripting fundamentals (variables, conditionals, loops, functions, exit codes)
Environment variables (PATH, HOME, export, .bashrc vs .bash_profile, /etc/environment)
Text processing tools (grep, sed, awk, cut, sort, uniq, tr, xargs)
Task scheduling (cron, crontab, at, systemd timers, anacron)
Regular expressions for pattern matching and data extraction
Version control basics (git init, add, commit, push, pull, branching)
Infrastructure automation concepts (Ansible basics, shell script deployment patterns)
domains.mastery_signal: Can write a bash script that parses log files, extracts error patterns with grep/awk, emails a summary via cron, and handles edge cases — without cargo-culting from Stack Overflow

domains.name: Troubleshooting
concepts: System performance analysis (top, vmstat, iostat, sar, free, df, du)
Network troubleshooting (ip, ss, ping, traceroute, dig, netstat, tcpdump, NetworkManager)
Storage troubleshooting (disk full, inode exhaustion, fsck, SMART monitoring, I/O bottlenecks)
Boot process troubleshooting (GRUB rescue, emergency/rescue targets, dracut, initramfs rebuild)
Log analysis and correlation (journalctl filters, /var/log/messages, syslog priorities, dmesg)
Service and application troubleshooting (dependency failures, port conflicts, resource exhaustion)
CPU and memory issues (runaway processes, OOM killer, memory leaks, load averages)
SELinux/AppArmor troubleshooting (audit2why, audit2allow, context mismatches)
domains.mastery_signal: Given a server that won't boot, can work through GRUB rescue to single-user mode, identify the failed service, check logs, fix the root cause, and get it back online — then explain every step to a junior admin

real_world_application: Administer Linux systems, automate tasks with scripts, and troubleshoot server and desktop environments
